title: Before picture-text statistics can run: none of the first six annotated folios is AGREED, and most of the measured disagreement is wording, not what the seats saw; a fixed vocabulary is needed first
statement: P-L4-013 counts only folios whose picture annotations are AGREED. I measured where that stands on the record at commit d28440e, using vs/registry.py's own picture_agreement on the 21 merged annotations (V-001 to V-021) of six folios, three or four seats each; five of the 21 are mine, and I read the others only after submitting my own. Result: no folio is AGREED. Best pairwise agreement per folio: f70v2 0.747, f75v 0.653, f67r2 0.614, f72r3 0.495, f66r 0.474, f99r 0.398; three folios stand as DISAGREE and three as DRAFT. Where the loss comes from, summed over all 596 matched object pairs: the kind agrees in 537 (90%). Features with a closed set of values agree almost always: cheeks 60/60, sex 40/40, facing 12/12, crescent_colour 12/12, ring 219/270, clothing 113/151. Features written as free phrases almost never match as strings although the seats describe the same thing: star 0/177 (one seat writes 'yes', one 'true', one 'attached'), posture 10/246 ('half figure standing in a tub' against 'upper body rising from an upright tub'), position 7/205, shape 4/116 ('disc with crescent' against 'round face inside a crescent'), note 0/13. Colour agrees in only 100/338 partly for the same reason ('uncoloured' against 'ink only, red dots on cheeks') and partly from real differences (on f99r one seat's 'orange' is another's 'red' or 'tan'). The five seats used 144 distinct feature keys, 105 of them used by one seat only, so most recorded features are never compared at all. Second cause: object matching. Only 209 of the 596 pairs were matched by label locus; seven of the 21 annotations give a label to at most one object, so their objects are paired by kind in list order, which pairs unrelated figures whenever two seats walk a ring from different starting points or in different directions (f72r3 ring feature: 5/30 and 6/30 in two pairs for that reason). What simple repairs buy, recomputed on the same data: leaving 'position' and 'note' out of the comparison lifts only f70v2 over the line (best pair 0.856); the other best pairs become f75v 0.731, f67r2 0.643, f99r 0.558, f66r 0.600, f72r3 0.528. Counting two values as equal when half their words overlap gives f99r 0.779, f75v 0.750, f66r 0.667 and leaves the rest unchanged. So neither repair alone makes the picture data usable; a shared vocabulary and a shared walking order are needed. I have not looked at whether any label words agree with pictures; this note concerns only the picture data. My own annotations share the fault: I wrote free phrases under 'form', 'position' and 'note' and assumed a ring starting point without a stated convention. Addition on the walking order, found afterwards: the ZL transcription itself records where each zodiac figure label stands. 299 of its label lines, all on the twelve zodiac pages plus one on f57v, carry a clock-position comment, and on every zodiac page each ring's first label is placed between about 8:45 and 11:30, never at 12 o'clock. So my own wheel annotations, which number ring figures clockwise from the figure nearest 12 o'clock and give the n-th figure the n-th label line, are rotated against the transcription by roughly one to three figures per ring (f70v2, f72r3, and the pending f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v); any other seat that assumed a 12 o'clock start has the same offset. Their label assignments on those rings should not be used as they stand. The repair is cheap: have annotators record each ring figure's clock position on the upright page, and match figures to label lines by ring and nearest clock position from the transcription's comments instead of by list order. Measured on one page: for f70v2 I took the positions of the 29 ring figures that I had noted from the scan when annotating (centre of the wheel at about 2008,1757 on canvas 1006200) and turned them into angles clockwise from the top. Each figure then falls within 17 degrees of exactly one label line's recorded clock position (23 of the 29 within 6 degrees, the worst three 12, 13 and 17), and the pairing is one to one. Against that, my merged annotation V-006 is rotated by three places in the outer ring and one in the inner: the figure I called outer-1 (my label f70v2.2) stands at f70v2.5, outer-2 at f70v2.6, and so on to outer-16 at f70v2.20, then outer-17, 18, 19 at f70v2.2, 3, 4; inner-1 to inner-9 stand at f70v2.23 to f70v2.31 and inner-10 at f70v2.22. Read V-006's ring labels with that correction. Its statement also says eight consecutive outer figures wear blue head coverings; its own object list records six (outer-4 and outer-6 to outer-10, that is label lines f70v2.8 and f70v2.10 to f70v2.14 after correction). The agreement of the angles with the transcription's clock positions, to a few degrees over 29 figures, shows the matching by clock position works on the public scans, as the code proposed on branch code-P-L4-013-fleet-opus assumes. The same matching applied to the one ring figure with a distinctive feature on my other merged wheel, f72r3 (V-011): the crowned figure of the inner ring stands at about 99 degrees clockwise from the top (figure at about 7470,1540 and wheel centre at about 7001,1464 on canvas 1006203), 9 degrees from the clock position recorded for label line f72r3.30 and 54 from the next nearest; V-011 gives it f72r3.29, so the crown belongs with f72r3.30. On the pending f72v1 annotation the crowned outer figure stands at about 10 degrees, between the positions recorded for f72v1.7 and f72v1.9, and the comment on f72v1.8 (01:45, out of sequence between 11:30 and 01:00) looks like a slip, so I leave that one undecided.
check: 1. Reproduce the numbers: at commit d28440e run vs.registry.read('picture') and picture_agreement on every pair of seats per folio; tally string equality per feature key. 2. Proposed repair, as a 'code:' pull request for a person to review (I do not make it here): a closed vocabulary per object kind in join.txt and the validator, for example human_figure: sex female|male|unclear, clothing nude|clothed, posture standing|half_in_tub|lying|inverted, container none|tub, headdress none|band|crown|veil|cap, star yes|no; star: points as an integer, tail yes|no; colours from a fixed list with 'none' for ink only; free description allowed only under 'note', which is not compared; a label locus required for every object that has a label line; and for ring figures a recorded clock position on the upright page, matched to the transcription's clock-position comments, in place of any assumed starting figure. 3. Then have the PIC steps for these six folios re-coded under the vocabulary by seats that have not yet annotated them, and require agreement of at least 0.8 with at least ten compared features before P-L4-013's statistics read a folio.
